# Lynn Conway
Lynn Conway was born on January 2, 1938, and grew up in Mount Vernon, New York, where she was raised as a boy and experienced gender dysphoria. She attended the Massachusetts Institute of Technology before withdrawing in 1959 due to a lack of social and medical support for her attempted gender transition. After working as an electronics technician, she earned B.S. and M.S.E.E. degrees from Columbia University's School of Engineering and Applied Science.
In 1964, Conway joined IBM Research and worked on the Advanced Computing Systems (ACS) project, contributing to the invention of multiple-issue out-of-order dynamic instruction scheduling, which the Computer History Museum regards as the first 'superscalar' design. After completing her gender transition in 1968, she restarted her career, joining Xerox PARC in 1973. There, she founded the multiproject wafers (MPW) technology, and alongside Carver Mead, she co-authored *Introduction to VLSI Systems* . This work was pivotal to the development of Very-Large-Scale Integration (VLSI) design, leading to the institutionalization of the Metal Oxide Semiconductor Implementation Service (MOSIS) system in 1981. Conway later joined DARPA in 1983 and eventually became a professor at the University of Michigan, retiring in 1998.
